title: Deep CNN Discovers 72 Missed Fast Radio Bursts From Repeating Source FRB 121102
aiSystem: Breakthrough Listen Deep Convolutional Neural Network (ResNet)
whyItMatters: Uncovered 72 previously missed extragalactic fast radio bursts in archival Green Bank Telescope observations of FRB 121102—more than quadrupling the single-observation yield—and constrained burst periodicity.
summary: Yunfan Gerry Zhang, Vishal Gajjar, Griffin Foster, Andrew Siemion, and the Breakthrough Listen team (UC Berkeley) applied a deep convolutional neural network to 400 TB of archival C-band Green Bank Telescope data from repeating fast radio burst source FRB 121102 (located 3 billion light-years away). Published in The Astrophysical Journal (2018), the CNN discovered 72 faint bursts missed by standard brute-force dedispersion pipelines—raising the 5-hour total from 21 to 93 bursts—and enabled a Rayleigh periodicity analysis ruling out constant arrival periods above 10 milliseconds at 99% confidence.
technicalHighlights: CNN trained on simulated and real dynamic spectra outperformed classical brute-force dedispersion in sensitivity, false-positive rate, and speed.
Discovered 72 new pulses from FRB 121102 in a single 5-hour Green Bank observation (bringing total detections from 21 to 93, including 45 in the first 30 minutes).
Used the expanded burst catalog to rule out constant arrival-time periodicity >10 ms with 99% confidence, sharpening magnetar and compact-object models.
caveats: CNN sensitivity depends on training-set coverage of dispersion-measure and frequency-drift morphologies, and candidate detections still underwent physical dedispersion verification.

scoreRationale.foundational: Landmark proof that deep vision models extract faint astrophysical transients invisible to classical radio-astronomy search pipelines.
scoreRationale.ripple: Catalyzed real-time deep-learning FRB and pulsar transient triggers across CHIME, FAST, MeerKAT, and SKA pathfinders.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in The Astrophysical Journal with every neural candidate physically confirmed via dedispersion.
scoreRationale.velocity: Re-mined 400 TB of archival telescope data to quadruple burst yield without a single extra hour of telescope time.

sources.label: The Astrophysical Journal (2018): Fast Radio Burst 121102 Pulse Detection and Periodicity: A Machine Learning Approach
